lines: Your emergency fund holds 3,600 dollars at 4 percent APY. Your cousin Ana saved the same 3,600 dollars at a big bank paying 0.01 percent. In one year you earn 144 dollars. She earns 36 cents.
APY is the share of your balance you earn in one year, with compounding already counted. It's the fair number to compare. Always compare APY to APY.
The FDIC says the average savings rate was 0.38 percent in October 2026. On 3,600 dollars that's 13 dollars and 68 cents a year. At 4 percent you get 130 dollars and 32 cents more.
Online banks can pay more because they don't pay for branches. A high-yield savings account pays many times the average.
Check the insurance first. FDIC at a bank, NCUA at a credit union. Both protect up to 250,000 dollars per person, per bank.
Read the fine print. Rates can change. Teaser rates end. And a 5 dollar monthly fee turns 144 dollars of interest into 84.
Moving money between banks takes 1 to 3 business days, so keep a small cushion in checking.
Interest is income. The bank sends a 1099-INT. In the 12 percent bracket you pay 17 dollars and 28 cents and keep 126 dollars and 72 cents.
Two seeds, same soil, same water. The one in the sun grows far faster. Your money is the seed, and the rate is the sunlight. Same safety, more growth.
